title: lux.toml
description:
The TOML manifest for a Lux project.

`lux.toml` is a subset of the [Lua rockspec format](https://github.com/luarocks/luarocks/blob/main/docs/rockspec_format.md),
with some simplifications, represented in TOML.
It does not support advanced specifications like platform overrides.
Those can be declared with an [`extra.rockspec`](https://lux.lumen-labs.org/guides/rockspec).

package.description: The name of the rock. Lux converts it to lower case when publishing.

version.description:
The package version. If unset, Lux derives it from the current SemVer
git tag (optional `v` prefix), falling back to "dev".

Versions like `1.0` are corrected to `1.0.0`.
Non-SemVer versions (e.g. `1.0-rc1` instead of `1.0.0-rc1`) are treated
as Dev versions and cannot be compared with SemVer versions.

build.description:
How to build the project. See the build backend fields below.

Rocks with C sources require a C compiler. Lux does not bundle one.

rockspec_format.description:
The LuaRocks rockspec format version to write to the generated rockspec ("1.0", "2.0", or "3.0").
Default: "3.0".

run.description: How to run the project with `lx run`.

lua.description:
The Lua version requirement, e.g. ">= 5.1". Required to build a rockspec.
Set to "luau" to build and run the project with Luau.

description.x-lux-toml-example:
[description]
summary = "A one-line description of the package"
detailed = """
A longer description of the package
that often spans multiple lines.
"""
license = "GPLv2"
homepage = "https://lumen-oss.github.io"
issues_url = "https://github.com/lumen-oss/lux/issues"
maintainer = "neorocks org"
labels = ["neovim", "tls", "https"]

supported_platforms.description:
Platforms this rock supports, mapping platform identifiers to `true` or
`false` (e.g. `linux = true`).

dependencies.description:
Runtime Lua dependencies, mapping package names to a version requirement
(e.g. `foo = "1.0"`) or to a detailed table with `version`, `opt`, `pin`,
`git`, `rev`, and `path` keys.

Version requirements support the operators `==`, `~=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`,
`>=`, and `~>`. `~> 2` means `>= 2, < 3`. An operator is optional;
without one, the requirement is treated as `==`. Version requirements
are mandatory.

Dependencies are declared under `lua`, `[dependencies]`,
`[build_dependencies]`, `[test_dependencies]`, and
`[external_dependencies]`.

Git dependencies support the `github:` (default), `gitlab:`,
`codeberg:`, and `sourcehut:` shorthands, as well as full HTTPS and SSH
URLs. If `rev` is unset, `version` is used as the commit SHA or tag.
Lux searches the repository root for a `lux.toml` or `.rockspec` to
determine the build specification, defaulting to `builtin` if none is
found. Rocks with git dependencies cannot be published to LuaRocks. Git
dependencies that require a custom LuaRocks build backend are not
supported.
dependencies.x-lux-toml-example:
[dependencies]
luafilesystem = "1.0.0"

[dependencies.argparse]
version = "0.7"
opt = true

[dependencies.foo]
version = "09511782201302ade916d4b250d01a6c61b56844"
git = "github:lunarmodules/foo"

[dependencies.bar]
path = "../bar"
version = "1.0.0"

build_dependencies.description: Dependencies needed at build time. Same syntax as `dependencies`.

external_dependencies.description:
System (C/FFI) dependencies, discovered via pkg-config. Each entry may
set `header` and/or `library`.

test_dependencies.description: Dependencies needed when running `lx test`. Same syntax as `dependencies`.

source.description:
Templates for generating the source URL of a release.

Variable substitutions:
- `$(PACKAGE)`: package name
- `$(VERSION)`: package version (from the git tag if not declared)
- `$(REF)`: git tag or revision (priority: SemVer tag, tag, commit SHA)
- `$(<VAR_NAME>)`: any environment variable

test.description:
How to run the test suite with `lx test`.

The `busted` backend is used when a `.busted` file exists and no backend
is specified. `busted-nlua` is used when a `.busted` file exists or
`busted` and `nlua` are `test_dependencies`. The `busted-nlua` backend is
currently broken on macOS and Windows. Luau projects default to `tiniest`.

project.description: Lux-specific project settings, ignored when generating a rockspec.

PackageName.description: A luarocks package name, which is always lowercase

type.description:
The build backend to use: "builtin", "make", "cmake",
"command", "none", "rust-mlua", "rust-binary", or "treesitter-parser".
Any other value is treated as a custom LuaRocks build backend.
Default: "builtin".

`make` requires Make, `cmake` requires CMake, and `rust-mlua`/`rust-binary`
require a Rust toolchain. Set `type = "none"` to copy source files
without building.

For Luau projects, `builtin` auto-detects `.luau` modules. Native
dependencies are not supported. Luau modules are transpiled to Lua when
the project targets a Lua runtime.

modules.description:
Modules to build, mapping module names (as used by `require`) to a source
path, a list of C sources, or a table with `sources`, `libraries`,
`defines`, `incdirs`, and `libdirs`.

makefile.description: Makefile to use. Default: "Makefile" ("Makefile.win" on Windows).

build_target.description: Target passed to `make` during the build pass. Default: empty.

build_pass.description: Whether to perform a build pass. Default: `true`.

install_target.description: Target passed to `make` during the install pass. Default: "install".

install_pass.description: Whether to perform an install pass. Default: `true`.

build_variables.description: Make variable assignments for the build pass.

install_variables.description: Make variable assignments for the install pass.

variables.description: Make or CMake variable assignments applied to both passes.

cmake.description:
Contents of the generated "CMakeLists.txt". If unset, the project's own
file is used.

Environment variables: `CMAKE_MODULE_PATH`, `CMAKE_INCLUDE_PATH`,
`CMAKE_LIBRARY_PATH`.

build_command.description: Command to run to build the package.

install_command.description: Command to run to install the package.

copy_directories.description:
Directories in the source tree to copy as-is into the rock's "etc" tree.
Do not use "lua", "lib", "rock_manifest", or the rockspec file name.

patches.description:
Patches to apply before building, mapping file names to patch contents.
Lux accepts any format supported by the [`diffy`](https://docs.rs/diffy/latest/diffy/) crate.
LuaRocks only supports unified diff.

target_path.description: The cargo target directory, if it is not `<source>/target`.
target_path.x-lux-toml-example:
[build]
type = "rust-mlua"
target_path = "target"
default_features = false
features = []
cargo_extra_args = []

[build.modules]
"foo.main" = "alt_name"

[build.include]
"relative/path/to/file.lua" = "target-file.lua"

default_features.description: Whether to build a cargo package with default features. Default: `true`.

cargo_extra_args.description: Additional arguments to pass to cargo.

package.description:
The cargo package to build.
Required for "rust-binary" in multi-package workspaces.

include.description:
Additional files to copy into the rock's "lua" directory, mapping source
paths to destinations.

lang.description: The parser language, e.g. "haskell". Required for "treesitter-parser".
lang.x-lux-toml-example:
[build]
type = "treesitter-parser"
lang = "haskell"
parser = true
generate = true
location = "libs/tree-sitter-haskell"

[build.queries."highlights.scm"] = """
(signature
  name: (variable) @function)
"""

parser.description:
Whether to build the tree-sitter parser. Set to `false` for query-only packages.
Default: `false`.

generate.description:
Whether to generate the tree-sitter parser sources before building.
Default: `false`.

location.description: Location of the tree-sitter grammar, relative to the source root.

queries.description:
Embedded queries to install into "etc/queries", mapping file names to
contents.

ModuleSpec.description:
A `build.modules` entry: a source path, a list of source paths, or a
table describing a compiled module.

anyOf.description: A path to a Lua or C source file.
A list of C source files.
A table describing a compiled module.

InstallSpec.description:
For packages which don't provide means to install modules
and expect the user to copy the .lua or library files by hand to the proper locations.
This struct contains categories of files. Each category is itself a table,
where the array part is a list of filenames to be copied.
For module directories only, in the hash part, other keys are identifiers in Lua module format,
to indicate which subdirectory the file should be copied to.
For example, lua = {["foo.bar"] = "src/bar.lua"} will copy src/bar.lua
to the foo directory under the rock's Lua files directory.

lib.description: Dynamic libraries implemented compiled Lua modules.

command.description: The command to execute when running the project

args.description: Arguments to pass to the command

RockDescription.description: A rock's metadata, to be displayed on the remote package server

summary.description: A one-line description of the package.

detailed.description: A longer description of the package.

license.description: The license used by the package.

homepage.description: An URL for the project. This is not the URL for the tarball, but the address of a website.

issues_url.description: An URL for the project's issue tracker.

maintainer.description: Contact information for the rockspec maintainer.

labels.description: A list of short strings that specify labels for categorization of this rock.

DependencyEntry.description:
A single `[dependencies]`-style entry: either a bare version requirement
or a detailed table.

version.description:
The version requirement, e.g. "1.0".
Supports the same operators as `dependencies`.

opt.description: Whether the dependency is optional. Default: `false`.

pin.description: Whether the dependency should be pinned. Default: `false`.

git.description:
A git source. Supported shorthands: "github:owner/repo" (default if the
prefix is omitted), "gitlab:owner/repo", "codeberg:owner/repo", and
"sourcehut:owner/repo". Full HTTPS and SSH URLs are also accepted.
If `rev` is unset, `version` is used as the commit SHA or tag.
Git dependencies cannot be published to LuaRocks.

rev.description: A commit SHA or tag to check out, separate from `version`.

ExternalDependencySpec.description: Can be defined in a [platform-agnostic](https://github.com/luarocks/luarocks/wiki/platform-agnostic-external-dependencies) manner

RockSourceTemplate.description:
Template for generating a remote rockspec source

Variables that can be substituted in each of the fields:
- `$(PACKAGE)`: Package name
- `$(VERSION)`: Package version
- `$(REF)`: Git tag or revision (prioritising tags if present)

Fields can also be substituted with environment variables.

file.description:
File name of the source archive.
Can be omitted if it can be inferred from the generated URL.

dir.description:
Name of the directory created when the source archive is unpacked.
Can be omitted if it can be inferred from the `file` field.

tag.description:
The tag or revision to be checked out if the source URL is a git source.
If unset, Lux will try to auto-detect it.

branch.description: The branch to be checked out if the source URL is a git source.

type.description:
The test backend: "busted", "busted-nlua", "tiniest", or "command".
If unset, Lux auto-detects a backend (e.g. "busted" when a ".busted"
file or the "busted" dependency is present).

flags.description: Extra CLI flags to pass to the test backend.

command.description: Shell command to run as the test suite. Mutually exclusive with `script`.

script.description: Lua script to run as the test suite. Mutually exclusive with `command`.

DeploySpec.description:
An undocumented part of the rockspec format.

Specifies additional install options

wrap_bin_scripts.description:
Whether to wrap installed Lua bin scripts to be executed with
the detected or configured Lua installation.
Defaults to `true`.

ProjectSpec.description:
Lux-specific project configuration.

This is not part of the rockspec format and is ignored when generating a rockspec.

root_dir.description:
The project root directory, relative to the directory containing the `lux.toml`.
Useful for multi-project workspaces, where the build files
(e.g. the cargo workspace `Cargo.toml`) do not live next to the `lux.toml`.
